turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve been having intermittent flank pain for about five months, and over the past two years I’ve had five urinary tract infections. I haven’t had any recent fever, weight loss, or noticeable changes in my urinary or bowel habits.
Can you describe the character of your flank pain—is it sharp and cramping in waves (colicky), or more of a constant dull ache? Does it radiate to your groin or lower abdomen?

Patient: It’s usually a dull ache, sometimes it comes and goes in a way that feels crampy, but not like severe waves. It doesn’t really radiate to my groin or lower abdomen—I mostly feel it in my side.
Have you noticed any blood in your urine—either visible pink/red urine or brown/tea-colored urine—especially during or after these pain episodes?
Patient: I haven’t noticed any visible blood in my urine, and I don’t recall any brown or tea-colored urine during or after the pain episodes.

Have you ever had imaging of your kidneys (such as an ultrasound or CT scan) during your previous UTI evaluations, and were you told you have kidney stones or any structural abnormalities of your urinary tract?
Patient: I haven’t had any kidney imaging like ultrasound or CT during my past UTI workups, and I wasn’t told I had kidney stones or any structural abnormalities.
What is your age and sex, and do these episodes of flank pain tend to occur at the same time as your urinary tract infections, or do they happen independently?

Patient: I’m 31, and I’m female. The flank pain doesn’t always occur exactly when I have a urinary tract infection—it’s more intermittent and seems to happen independently at times, though there’s been overlap.
Do these episodes of flank pain have any relationship to your menstrual cycle, or do you experience severe menstrual cramps, pain with intercourse, or unusual bleeding patterns?
Patient: I haven’t noticed a clear relationship to my menstrual cycle, and I don’t have severe cramps. I also don’t experience pain with intercourse or any unusual bleeding patterns.
Does the flank pain ever get worse after you drink a large amount of fluids, or do you ever experience nausea or vomiting during these episodes?
Patient: I don’t think the pain gets worse after drinking more fluids, and I haven’t had nausea or vomiting with these episodes.
Is the flank pain located on one specific side (left or right), or does it affect both sides?

Doctor: Is the flank pain located on one specific side (left or right), or does it affect both sides? Patient: It’s usually on one side at a time—mostly on the left, though it can occasionally switch. I don’t feel it equally on both sides simultaneously.
Were your previous urinary tract infections confirmed with urine cultures showing bacteria, or were they diagnosed based on symptoms alone?

Patient: I’m not sure if they did urine cultures—I was told I had UTIs based on my symptoms and urinalysis results, and I was treated with antibiotics each time. I don’t recall being told what specific bacteria were found.
During your previous UTI episodes, did you experience fever, chills, or nausea—suggesting the infection may have reached your kidneys (pyelonephritis)?
“I haven’t had fever, chills, or nausea with the flank pain episodes. It’s mainly a dull ache that sometimes feels crampy, and it stays in my side without spreading elsewhere.”

When you have the pain, if you or someone taps firmly with a fist over that exact spot on your back (over the kidney area), does it cause sharp, significant pain—more so than tapping other areas of your back?

Patient: Yes, when it’s happening, pressing or tapping firmly over that spot on my back tends to make the pain feel sharper and more noticeable than other parts of my back. I don’t have fever or chills with it.

Patient: I mainly feel it as a side flank ache that gets sharper when that specific kidney-area spot is pressed, and it hasn’t come with fever, chills, or nausea. It’s been going on intermittently for about five months and sometimes overlaps with my past UTI episodes. I haven’t had imaging or been told I have stones or a structural issue.
Do you have diabetes, or have you experienced symptoms like excessive thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained fatigue?

Patient: No, I don’t have diabetes, and I haven’t had excessive thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained fatigue. My main issue is the intermittent side flank pain that feels sharper when that specific kidney-area spot is pressed.
